v.why: With e0 absent, e3 is often the only live path to the output, so deleting it collapses the cell (e.g., #8, #32, #360).
When e0 is none, node 2 depends solely on e1, so removing e1 kills the node-2 branch (e.g., #38, #365, #400).
If e1 is none, e0 feeds both intermediate nodes, so removing it leaves only the direct e3 path (e.g., #75, #114, #144).
Replacing a parameter-free pool on the direct input-output edge with a conv adds substantial capacity (e.g., #162, #175, #183).
Swapping avg_pool for a learnable conv on edge 3 gives large gains (e.g., #92, #182, #337).
A skip on the direct path beats pooling there, whereas replacing a conv with skip loses capacity (e.g., #59, #88, #309).
Turning a learnable conv on the direct edge into pooling strongly hurts (e.g., #212, #186, #248).
Adding a pool where there was no edge opens a new path, while replacing a conv with pool removes capacity (e.g., #70, #54, #247).
Adding a skip where e5 was absent connects node 2 to the output instead of degrading a conv (e.g., #55, #321).
Replacing an identity on the node2-output edge with a conv adds a learnable transform and gives large gains (e.g., #22, #25).

raw:
Ten hypotheses, chosen from the 400 measured edits and from how the cell is wired. Node 3 sums e3(x0), e4(node1) and e5(node2). Node 1 is fed only by e0. Node 2 is fed by e1 and e2.

1. **Removing e3 hurts much more when e0 = none.** Without e0, e3 is often the only path left to the output. Experiments #8, #32 and #360 show drops of 15 to 79 pp.
2. **Removing e1 hurts much more when e0 = none.** Without e0, node 2 relies on e1 as its only input. See #38, #365 and #400.
3. **Removing e0 hurts more when e1 = none.** Then node 1 and node 2 lose their only input. See #75, #114 and #144.
4. **Changing e3 to nor_conv_3x3 helps more when e3 was avg_pool_3x3.** A parameter-free pool on the direct path is swapped for a learnable conv. See #162, #175, #183 and #145.
5. **Changing e3 to nor_conv_1x1 helps more when e3 was avg_pool_3x3.** Same reasoning. See #92, #182, #337 and #136.
6. **Changing e3 to skip_connect helps more when e3 was avg_pool_3x3.** A skip on the input-to-output edge beats pooling. See #59, #88, #165 and #309.
7. **Changing e3 to avg_pool_3x3 hurts more when e3 was nor_conv_1x1.** It destroys a learnable path. See #212, #186, #248 and #127.
8. **Changing e5 to avg_pool_3x3 does better when e5 was none.** It adds a path instead of downgrading a conv. See #70, #54 and #247, against large losses in #12, #322 and #330.
9. **Changing e5 to skip_connect does better when e5 was none.** It adds a path instead of replacing a conv. See #55 and #321, against #160 and #316.
10. **Changing e5 to nor_conv_1x1 helps more when e5 was skip_connect.** It adds a learnable transform where there was only identity. See #22 and #25 (+8 to +9 pp), against smaller gains elsewhere.
